newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher on moderate volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher on moderate volumes.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher across the board Friday, on moderate volumes, with nearby active September palladium registering a new contract high.
"Gold and silver are choppy, with influential speculators going long in the morning and taking profits in the afternoon this week," PaineWebber analyst Bernard Savaiko said.

"I wouldn't start thinking about getting short down here, but my gut feeling is gold is going to go down and test the lows and maybe break them by a small margin, as it's first notice day in August gold next week, and the contract may get a good hit in that time frame, " he said.
"Gold may still be oversold, but the question is where is it going to go on the upside with stocks, bonds and dollar still strong."
COMEX August gold ended up $2.70 an ounce at $326.50, after trading a $323.50-328.00 range, compared with Thursday's range of $321.20-329.70.
The August/December spread ended wider at $3.60 an ounce, from a low of $3.10 on Wednesday and $3.30 Thursday.
December gold is now the more active contract, with open interest of 69,721 contracts, compared to 55,939 contracts in August gold.
Total COMEX gold open interest rose 1,586 lots Thursday to 207,793 contracts, after open interest declined in the past week from 18 month highs at 222,069 on July 16.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $325.75/25, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $324.10 and the New York close Thursday around $324.50/00.

Gold prices have been consolidating in the past two weeks after hitting a 12 year low in early July around $314.00 an ounce, following confirmation of a sale of 167 tonnes of gold by the Australian central bank.

Sharply lower gold prices have resulted in South Africa's Free State Consolidated Gold Mines FCM.J, a division of Anglo American Corp, warning of pit closures this week, while Canada's Echo Bay Mines Ltd is reported to have cut back on processing low grade reserves.

"This will reduce worldwide production at a time when total industrial and jewelry usage has been increasing substantially, thus raising the annual deficit between (mining) supply and demand," said Steven Jon Kaplan, editor of the "Gold Mining Outlook."

Meanwhile, COMEX September silver ended up 4.0 cents at $4.315 an ounce, with the September/December backing up to 6.5 cents, from 6.2 cents Thursday. September silver remains trapped in its $4.20-4.40 range, after spot silver saw three year lows earlier this month.
Platinum group metals (PGM) prices continued to recover steadily from the two month lows seen in early July, despite the resumption of Russian exports in the past week.
Japanese traders said the first Russian platinum shipments in six months arrived at Narita Airport in Tokyo late Thursday. The first palladium shipments arrived last week.
But the PGM forward price curves remain highly backwardated, with palladium sponge at around a $10.00 an ounce premium to Zurich ingot, traders said.
"PGMs supplies are still critically tight and the question is whether Russia will be able to meet the demand," Paine Webber's Savaiko said.

"The consensus is whatever the Russians ship this year will be less than year ago levels, and the fact that the Russians are going back into the spot market this week suggests they may be bypassing contractual obligations to get the highest price, which could be indication they may not have a lot to sell, especially in case of platinum."

NYMEX October platinum ended up $4.50 at $416.50 an ounce, with the October/January ending at $11.00 an ounce, after widening out to $17.00 an ounce intraday. The October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread widened to $88.40 an ounce.
NYMEX September palladium closed up $4.15 at $190.00 an ounce, after execution of a fund stop order on the open helped to push September palladium to a new life-of-contract high at $194.00.
